22.0.0.en: Since the eighth commandment forbade theft, here God decrees the penalty for the one who steals, which is restitution of four or five times as much, as a kind of discipline for the thief and to show the seriousness of the effect of his theft on others, by bringing fear and disturbance upon them, so that he must compensate them with more than he stole from them. And if the size and price of what was stolen increases, the compensation is greater (five oxen - four sheep). The greater the thief's greed, the greater the discipline he needs, with greater compensation, because the one who steals an ox is bolder in evil than others, besides the fact that he deprived its owners of the price of hiring it out or of using it in work, so the compensation for his theft is greater.

22.0.1.en: May you think about the effects of your sins on others so that you turn back from them, and then try to make up to others, not only with an apology but with words and deeds of love, so that you restore to them trust in you and peace of mind in dealing with you.

22.1.0.en: If the thief breaks through the wall or the door during the act of theft, and the owner of the goods senses him, rises to defend himself and strikes the thief so that he dies, the thief deserves this death because of his evil, and the owner of the house is not avenged upon or punished, because he was defending his property.

22.2.0.en: The sun be risen upon him: the thief continued trying to steal until daybreak, and then the owner of the goods can call to his neighbors and they can seize the thief, so he has no need to kill him in self-defense.

22.2.1.en: There shall be blood shed for him: that is, he is alive and can be seized alive, and it is not lawful to kill him.

22.2.2.en: He should make full restitution: the thief is punished by making restitution for what he was trying to steal. Since he had not taken it, slaughtered it or sold it, it says only that he shall make restitution and does not specify the amount of the restitution; this is determined by the judges, and it is usually double. If he have nothing: if he is poor and destitute.

22.2.3.en: Then he shall be sold for his theft: he is sold as a slave to the owner of the goods or to someone else, and the owner of the goods takes the price; and it is the right of the owner of the goods, if he takes him as a slave, to sell him to whomever he wishes if he does not see fit to keep him with him. This calls for not being hasty in killing the thief, and decrees that he be punished with restitution, and even if he is destitute, he sells himself as a slave to the owner of the goods.

22.3.0.en: If the thief is caught with the stolen goods in his hand and has not disposed of them by slaughtering or selling them, that is, he has not gone further in his greed and theft, he is disciplined by paying lesser compensation, which is double.

22.4.0.en: Here he speaks of unintentional theft that results from negligence, in the case of the shepherd who lets his sheep eat from his neighbor's field. Here he must compensate his neighbor with the best fruits of his own field, because he could have kept the sheep away but was merely negligent, that is, he took what was not his, namely the fruits of his brother's field.

22.5.0.en: If fire break out, and catch in thorns: if thorns or any wood or goods burn in someone's field.

22.5.1.en: So that the stacks of corn burn: the fire moved with the wind from the burning thorns to the neighbor's storehouses, where he keeps goods piled one upon another, of grain or anything else, and these stores burned. Or the standing corn, or the field: that is, crops that had begun to dry, or any goods that were in the field.

22.5.2.en: He that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution: the one who lit the fire and did not take care that it should not reach his neighbor is responsible for this negligence, and the judges decide on the appropriate compensation; but it will be less than for the one who was negligent with his sheep eating his neighbor's crops, because keeping sheep away is easier than stopping a fire.

22.6.0.en: If a man deliver to another silver or goods to keep as a trust for someone else, and it is stolen, and the thief is caught, this thief makes restitution of double only, because the stolen goods were found with him and he had not disposed of them.

22.7.0.en: If it is impossible to catch the thief, the one who was keeping the trust is brought before the judges to examine whether he stole this trust or it was stolen from him.

22.8.0.en: The cause of both parties: the one who deposited and the one with whom it was deposited, or the thief and the one robbed.

22.8.1.en: In the end he decrees the summary of the law of restitution, which is that anything stolen that is found with the thief is compensated for with two, after the judges examine him and decide that he is the thief. That is, if the one with whom the thing was deposited denies the deposited thing and his guilt is proved, he pays double; and the one who found something lost and denied it pays the owner of the lost thing double. And bringing their cause before God means bringing it before the elders so that they may judge who is the thief.

22.9.0.en: If a man delivers to another a trust such as an animal, and it dies, or is hurt, or is stolen from him, the owner of the animal and the trustee are brought to the court, and if it is proved that the trustee did not interfere, the owner of the animal receives no compensation at all, because he was faithful over the animal.

22.9.1.en: No man seeing it: there was no witness who saw what happened to the animal.

22.9.2.en: The oath of the LORD: he raises his right hand and swears by the truth.

22.10.0.en: If the animal deposited with the trustee is stolen because he was careless in guarding it, he makes restitution for it since it was stolen, because he was negligent in watching over it. But if it was stolen while grazing in the wilderness by some passing traveler without the trustee seeing, he makes no compensation at all, as stated in (v. 10).

22.11.0.en: If a wild beast attacks the deposited animal and kills it, the trustee presents evidence proving that it was torn, which is the testimony of witnesses or parts of the animal's body that the beast left behind, and this evidence is presented to the court, so the owner of the animal receives no compensation.

22.12.0.en: If a person borrows anything and it is lost or broken, and the owner of this thing is rich and not in need, he does not compensate him for what was damaged. But if the owner of the thing is in need, the borrower must compensate him.

22.12.1.en: And if a man hires anything and the thing he hired is lost or broken, he does not compensate its owner, because he paid the hire for this thing, and this hire compensates for any damage that may occur.

22.13.0.en: Entice: he showed affection for the purpose of fornication.

22.13.1.en: If a man approaches a virgin and influences her emotionally until he commits fornication with her, he must bear his responsibility, marry her, and pay her father the dowry, the amount customarily paid in such cases according to custom and society, which is fifty shekels of silver (Deut 22:29). It is noted that this amount is more than the usual amount in a dowry because he sinned against a virgin; and if he marries her, he does not divorce her, that is, he is bound to his new marriage. Here he deals with the problem through a positive act, which is marriage.

22.13.2.en: But if the girl was betrothed and committed fornication with the man of her own will, both are stoned; but if the man raped her, that is, she was the one wronged, the man who assaulted her is stoned alone (Deut 22:23-27).

22.14.0.en: If a man commits fornication with a virgin and wants to marry her but her father refuses, he is bound to pay the dowry as compensation for his offense against her.

22.15.0.en: Sorcery is considered dealing with demons and submission to them, and it also draws souls to deal with them; so it is spiritual fornication and a promotion of fornication by causing others to fall. That is, sorcery is a rejection of faith in God and a resort to another power, which is Satan, the adversary of God; therefore the Law commands that sorcerers be put to death. It says "a witch" because most of those who practiced sorcery at that time were women (1 Sam 28:7, Acts 16:16).

22.15.1.en: The sin of causing others to stumble is a hideous sin, for it makes others fall into evil; so instead of a person striving for good and drawing souls to God, he makes light of them and of their salvation. Therefore be careful in your words and actions so that you do not cause anyone to stumble.

22.16.0.en: Fornication with animals is not an offense against a human being, but it is uncleanness and immersion in bodily pleasure. This sin was widespread among the Canaanites, among whom the children of Israel lived; therefore whoever does this is put to death, because it is considered uncleanness, it angers God, and it deserves death.

22.16.1.en: It is understood from this verse that uncleanness is an evil that greatly angers God, even if neither party complains; so if two agree to commit fornication, God is angry at their evil because it is uncleanness.

22.17.0.en: The worship of idols is spiritual fornication; therefore whoever does it is punished by death.

22.18.0.en: Do not exploit the stranger, because he knows no one in the place, so that you trouble him or oppress him and demand of him more than his duties; for lack of mercy greatly displeases God. And so that God may stir their feelings of mercy, He reminds them that they were strangers in Egypt for many long years, so that, recalling how hard the feelings of being a stranger are, they may have mercy on strangers.

22.19.0.en: The widow is the woman without a husband, that is, without support, and the fatherless is the one without a father, that is, without care; and so they always signify the need for mercy. Therefore wronging them is harder than wronging any ordinary person, and is considered a great injustice.

22.19.1.en: Care for the weak and the needy, have compassion on them, help them and bear with them because of their hard circumstances. And do not forget that you are the widow who has no support but God, and the fatherless who has no true father but God, and the stranger in this world who is poor of every virtue, so that you may be humbled and seek God's mercies, and this will move you to be merciful to everyone.

22.20.0.en: God declares His fatherhood and care for the weak in His attention to the prayers of the oppressed, such as the widow and the fatherless. If your oppression of the widow and the fatherless increases, He is angry with you, and enemies attack and kill the men, so that your wives become widows and your children fatherless, because you did not have compassion on the widow and the fatherless.

22.21.0.en: Another form of mercy is lending to the needy. He requires His people not to charge usury, that is, any interest on the amount borrowed, but it is enough that they take back the same amount, sharing with the needy person in the amount of interest they have given up. And of course, if feelings of mercy are stirred, a person can lend and not demand that the other repay what he borrowed; and it is better to help the needy from the beginning with the amount as a gift. Debts were released by their owner when the seventh year came (Deut 15:11-17), and it was permitted for the Jews to take usury from non-Jews (Deut 23:19, 20). But sadly the Jews abandoned this law, as is shown by what happened in the days of Elisha the prophet with the widow woman (2 Kgs 4:1).

22.22.0.en: Raiment: this is the outer garment that covers his body and keeps him warm during the night if he has no other covering.

22.22.1.en: If a poor man is compelled to pledge his garment because of his need for money, and walked naked that day and could not repay what he owed within the day, then before the going down of the sun, that is, after he has worked and received his wages and still could not repay, the one who took the garment must return it to him so that he may sleep in it, for how can he sleep naked when he may have no covering? And if he wrongs him and keeps the garment with him, then in his distress and need he cries out to God, and then He hears him, because He is merciful, and takes vengeance on the one who wronged him for exploiting the poor man.

22.22.2.en: God's mercies toward the needy also appear in what the Law prescribes, that it is not permitted to take a widow's garment in pledge because of her particular circumstances, but she borrows without pledging anything (Deut 24:17).

22.23.0.en: Another form of oppression is abuse. However troubled a person may be, he must not dare to revile God or the ruler of his people, but must endure, and he will understand afterward the reason for the affliction he is passing through, and perhaps the reason is his sin.

22.24.0.en: Man goes on and on in the sin of oppression, and is not content with oppressing human beings but dares to oppress God also:

22.24.1.en: First: by reviling God while murmuring (v. 28). Then, in this verse, by not offering the firstfruits, whether of the grain gathered on the threshing floor, or of the grapes and olives pressed in the winepress, or of the firstborn sons, for whom a ransom is offered, as mentioned in (ch. 13:13).

22.25.0.en: Likewise God requires them to offer the firstborn of animals such as cattle and sheep, and God's mercy appears in that the animal is taken only after seven days, so that it may suckle from its mother the basic milk that nourishes it, and out of respect for the mother's motherhood toward her suckling; this is compassion for the animal.

22.25.1.en: Offer the firstfruits and the tithes to receive God's blessing on all your possessions, and know that God does not need your gifts, but they are so that you may show your love for God, your sympathy with the poor and your care for the needs of the Church, and God will repay you with many blessings.

22.26.0.en: He forbids them to eat an animal torn by beasts, because it is unclean for two reasons:

22.26.1.en: (1) That it has been touched by an unclean animal, which is the predatory animal.

22.26.2.en: (2) That its blood did not come out of it but was held in it, so it becomes unclean.

22.26.3.en: And He commands them to cast it to the dogs. In this He calls them to holiness, not only in eating clean meat but in all their life, so that their hearts may be pure from evil and loving God.

22.26.4.en: Justice, the feasts, God's presence with them, and refusing to mingle with the wicked

23.0.0.en: Here He rejects the sin of lying by rejecting false reports, and therefore a person cannot bear false witness, for this is supporting false speech; that is, the Law calls him to reject lying in all its forms.

23.0.1.en: Do not make light of lying through exaggeration and overstatement or through understatement and belittling, but be careful in all your words and do not be hasty in them, and examine every report you hear, and God will guide you to distinguish truth from falsehood; and do not spread false talk without intending to, leading others astray and angering God.

23.1.0.en: He also warns against sharing in any evil by word or deed, and against supporting anything false, even if everyone agrees on it.

23.2.0.en: Do not pity the poor man because of his weak appearance and so pervert justice and wrong the rich man, but be just, and let the poor man be punished if he is in the wrong.

23.3.0.en: God calls them to help others, not only loved ones and relatives but enemies also. If an animal belonging to one of their enemies strays away from him and is lost and one of the Hebrews finds it, he must take hold of it and bring it back to the enemy. And if this was in the Law of the Old Testament, how much more in the New Testament we must love enemies and have compassion on them.

23.3.1.en: If your heart is filled with love, you will love every person, even if he wrongs you or is your enemy; for through love you become like Christ, you reach the Kingdom, you put your enemy to shame, and you break the evil that is in you and in him.

23.4.0.en: Wouldest forbear to help him: you refused to help your enemy.

23.4.1.en: Thou shalt surely help with him: you must help your enemy.

23.4.2.en: He gives another example of helping others and chooses an animal, the donkey, which carries loads and belongs to an enemy, and has fallen to the ground on the road under the weight of the load. He requires him to lift the load off the donkey and set it up so that it may continue its way; for lifting such loads is usually not done by one person but by two or more, that is, he helps the one who wrongs him to set his donkey on its feet.

23.5.0.en: He gives another example of helping others, which is helping the weak, such as the poor man. If he brings a suit before the judges to examine some problem, he must not join the rich in pressing the poor man so that he loses his case because he has no champion on account of his poverty, but must declare the truth and support the poor man and not pervert justice.

23.6.0.en: In helping others, He calls them to support the innocent and the righteous before the judges, so that he does not lie, that is, bear false witness, and wrong the innocent and kill him and justify the wicked; for God is not pleased with this, because playing with words, that is, lying, can mislead the court so that it wrongs the innocent and justifies the wicked.

23.6.1.en: Be careful in your words lest you suggest an accusation against the innocent or flatter the wicked because of his position or your embarrassment before him; but proclaim the voice of God gently and clearly even if it does not please the wicked, for God's pleasure with you is more important than people.

23.7.0.en: He also forbids, in their helping others, bribery, which influences a person to blind him to the truth, so that he looks for crooked ways and loopholes in the law to justify the one who gave him the bribe, and so loses his justice as a judge, since he becomes like a blind man who does not see the truth.

23.8.0.en: He asks them to help others in the case of strangers who have no support from others, and to remember that they were in need of help when they were strangers in Egypt, from the days of Joseph until Moses.

23.9.0.en: The Law also commands that the land be sown for six years and then be given rest in the seventh year, for several purposes:

23.9.1.en: 1- The poor eat from it the remains of the crops in it and the natural plants that grow in it.

23.9.2.en: 2- What is left after the poor is eaten by the animals.

23.9.3.en: 3- The land rests from the strain of cultivation to make up for what it has lost and prepare for sowing in the following year, and this is scientifically beneficial.

23.9.4.en: In addition to the spiritual benefits, which are:

23.9.5.en: 1- Faith in God and reliance on Him, because He promised to give double the harvest in the sixth year, which would suffice their needs for two years.

23.9.6.en: 2- An opportunity to devote themselves to the worship of God in the seventh year.

23.9.7.en: And when the children of Israel neglected to carry out the commandment of the seventh year, God punished them with captivity, so that by depriving them of their land for seventy years they would make up for what they had neglected in sanctifying the seventh year in the past, before the captivity (2 Chr 36:21).

23.10.0.en: The stranger: the foreigner who serves you and works for you.

23.10.1.en: The law of compassion also appears in the law of sanctifying the Sabbath day, for agricultural work is left on the Sabbath, and thus rest is given to the animals working in the cultivation of the land, and likewise to the slaves, in addition to the hired workers he hires from the Gentiles.

23.11.0.en: Here he summarizes what preceded, confirming the carrying out of the preceding commandments, the most important of which are the worship of God and the rejection of idols.

23.12.0.en: Here He sets out the three most important feasts of the Jews, which are.

23.12.1.en: The first feast is the Passover, the cause of their deliverance from the slavery of Egypt, and it is a type of the Lord Christ the crucified Redeemer. And the other two feasts are the harvest and the ingathering; for in the time of material joy we must thank God and glorify Him.

23.12.2.en: The feasts were mentioned in detail in (Lev 23, Num 18, 28).

23.13.0.en: The Passover is followed by the feast of unleavened bread, free of leaven, which they eat for seven days, and it signifies purity from all evil, which is signified by leaven. And He requires them to offer God's gifts in this feast as proof of their love for Him, and they keep the feast from the evening of the fourteenth day of the month of Abib (Nisan) until the evening of the twenty-first day of it.

23.13.1.en: And the month of Abib mentioned corresponds to the months of March and April, and it is different from the Abib found in the Coptic year.

23.13.2.en: Take care to offer something to God every day through worship and doing good, so that you do not stand before Him empty on this day, and on the last day you will find something to offer Him.

23.14.0.en: The feast of harvest (or the feast of Pentecost): this is the gathering of the crops that ripen at the beginning of the season, which are the winter crops such as wheat. This feast falls fifty days after the first Sunday after the Passover, and this Sunday was called the feast of firstfruits, and it was mentioned in detail in (Lev 23, Deut 16). The feast of ingathering (which is the feast of tabernacles): in it the crops that ripen late are gathered, that is, the summer crops such as grapes and olives, and its duration is a week beginning on the fifteenth of the seventh month (Ethanim). The people dwell in booths during this period in remembrance of their sojourning in the wilderness of Sinai, and it was mentioned in detail in (Lev 23, Deut 16). In these two feasts each one offers the firstfruits of what God has gathered, that He may bless the rest of the harvest gathered, and they are to be glad because God allowed them to give to Him, and likewise the needy rejoice, who are satisfied by these gifts.

23.15.0.en: God redeemed the firstborn of the children of Israel with the Passover lamb from the plague on the firstborn; therefore the males owe their lives to God and come in these feasts to thank Him and praise Him.

23.15.1.en: And the male represents his family and not only himself, so all the males come to keep the feast to God in these feasts. Of course women can also attend, but at least the males attend as representatives of their families to offer their gifts to God and thank Him because He saved them from slavery in Egypt and from death, just as we now thank God in the feasts because He saved us from the death of sin.

23.16.0.en: He commands them in the feast of the Passover that the sacrifice be accompanied by unleavened bread without leaven, because unleavened bread signifies the purity with which a person comes forward to receive God's salvation.

23.16.1.en: He also commands them not to leave any of the Passover sacrifice until the next day, as in (ch. 12); and in general the fat of any sacrifice offered to God is burned on the altar of burnt offering, for it is God's, and neither the priest nor the people eat of it, so the fat must be burned on the altar on the day the animal is slaughtered, that is, the part belonging to God is offered immediately after the sacrifice is slaughtered.

23.17.0.en: The house of the LORD: the tabernacle of the congregation or the temple of Solomon that was built later.

23.17.1.en: Here He stresses offering the firstfruits. And God's mercy appears in that they are not to boil a kid newly born that is still suckling from its mother; for God teaches us compassion toward animals so that we may have compassion all the more on our poor and weak brethren. In addition, it is His rejection of a pagan belief among the Gentiles that prescribed cooking a newborn kid in its mother's milk and then pouring out its broth on the fields to give fertility to the land. And in general the Law teaches a person not to cook the small slaughtered animal and eat it with its mother's milk, which was supposed to feed it so that it might live by it, so that he may learn compassion in all his dealings.

23.18.0.en: An Angel: what is meant by the angel here is a messenger, and he is either:

23.18.1.en: 1- A luminous angel who leads them on the way until the Promised Land.

23.18.2.en: 2- An angel who appears in the form of the pillar of fire or the pillar of cloud.

23.18.3.en: 3- God Himself who speaks with them, and what is meant is the Angel of the Covenant, that is, the Second Hypostasis, in the form of a voice speaking or a cloud appearing in the tabernacle of the congregation, showing His presence and being there.

23.19.0.en: He warns them so that they may obey this Angel, because he represents God or is God Himself, since He says My name is in him, and he will not pardon their sins if they persist in evil.

23.20.0.en: He promises them that if they obey the Angel, that is, obey God, He will defend them against their enemies, that is, they will walk in assurance in all their life.

23.21.0.en: He also promises them that the Angel will bring them to the Promised Land and will destroy the wicked peoples dwelling there so that they may dwell in their place. The destruction was complete or partial for some, that is, a small remnant of them remained according to the greatness of their evils; but God had commanded the destruction of all, yet the children of Israel were negligent in driving them out and killing them after Joshua.

23.21.1.en: Obedience to God's commandments protects you from the wars of the demons, so however hard they are, do not abandon them, but ask for His help that you may enjoy His care and love.

23.22.0.en: He also warns them against taking part in the worship of idols worshiped by the Gentiles in whose place they will dwell in the Promised Land, and moreover He asks them to tear down the walls and pillars and temples (their images) that they set up for their worship.

23.22.1.en: And if some object that killing these peoples involves cruelty, because they had no chance to know God, and what is the fault of their children who are killed, the answer to that is that:

23.22.2.en: 1- God speaks to all human beings through His voice within them, which is the conscience.

23.22.3.en: 2- Nature speaks of the existence of God and His oneness.

23.22.4.en: 3- These peoples had heard of what God did with His people, their crossing of the Red Sea and the ten plagues, and this was enough for them to believe in Him.

23.22.5.en: 4- There are examples of faith and life with God among the Gentiles, such as Rahab the harlot (Josh 2, 6:25) and Ruth.

23.22.6.en: 5- The death of the children was painful to their fathers, that perhaps they might repent, and God, by His foreknowledge, knows that these children would have become wicked. Likewise God will judge the children who did not sin in a way different from the wicked adults.

23.23.0.en: He stresses to them that they should worship God only, and then God will bless their bread and their water and protect them from diseases and heal them from them if they afflict them.

23.23.1.en: God's blessing rests upon you if you worship Him and your heart does not cling to the material things of the world; He then provides for your material needs, and you are not hindered by illnesses or the obstacles of the world from worshiping Him, so you live in joy all your days until you reach the Kingdom.

23.24.0.en: God also promises them, if they hold fast to His worship, to bless every pregnant woman so that her child is not lost, and to give offspring from all the wombs of its women, so there is no barren one, that is, they increase in number and strength. Then He also promises them length of days, confirming the increase of their number.

23.25.0.en: All the people to whom thou shalt come: the pagan peoples whom you attack and drive out because of their evil.

23.25.1.en: Turn their backs: they run and flee before you.

23.25.2.en: God adds also that He appears in His majesty in His war with the enemies, so they fear and flee quickly from before the children of Israel. And the awe of God appears either in the dignity of His children, so that the enemies fear them, or by some other means such as the hornets (v. 28) or thunder.

23.26.0.en: Hornets: plural of hornet, an insect that gives unbearable stings, which God sends before the children of Israel in their war with the original inhabitants of the Promised Land, so they flee from before them in the war (Josh 24:12, Wis 12:8, 9).

23.27.0.en: Here appears God's wisdom in driving out the enemies gradually, so that there may be an opportunity for the children of Israel to build up the cities in their place. But if He drove them out quickly, the wild beasts would come and dwell in their abandoned cities and the children of Israel could not enter them; and at the same time, driving out the peoples gradually was an opportunity for these peoples to repent and for some of their individuals at least to return to God (Wis 12:10-27).

23.27.1.en: Do not be troubled if your striving against any sin lasts long, for God removes it from you gradually so that you do not fall into pride or any other sins, for He knows the fierceness of the devil, and at the same time you have an opportunity for your faith to be established through spiritual striving and to be strengthened by the grace of God.

23.28.0.en: Another reason for driving out the enemies gradually is to give the children of Israel an opportunity to take care of cultivating the land, so that they eat of its fruits and enjoy them.

23.29.0.en: God defined for him the area of the Promised Land that he would possess, which extends southward from the Red Sea (the Sea of Suph) to the northwest, which is the Mediterranean Sea, that is, the sea of the Philistines; and from the wilderness, that is, the wilderness of Sinai in the southwest, to the river, which is the river Euphrates in the northeast. This actually happened in the days of David and Solomon (1 Kgs 4:21, 24). But in the New Testament the people of God are those who believe in Christ in every place in the world, and not within the area of a particular land.

23.30.0.en: He requires him not to make peace or covenant with the inhabitants of the land and dwell with them, but to drive them out, lest if he mingles with them he becomes bound to the worship of idols and leaves God; and this actually happened in the era of the Judges (Judg 2, 3). But whoever of the pagan peoples believes joins the people of God, like Uriah the Hittite and Araunah the Jebusite (2 Sam 11:3, 24:16). The covenant with God and Moses' ascent of the mountain
